verdict.rationale: Composio's trigger docs describe a registrable webhook URL per project. Composio POSTs every trigger event from connected apps (Slack messages, GitHub commits, emails) to it as a signed, structured payload, which is genuine outbound HTTP callback delivery. missing for 10: details on choosing which trigger events to subscribe to, retry/delivery-guarantee documentation, support for more than one destination per project, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: Composio delivers every event to one destination you control: your webhook URL. You register it once per project, and Composio `POST`s every trigger event there, signed so you can verify it.
When something happens in a connected app (a new Slack message, a GitHub commit, an incoming email), a trigger sends that event to your app as a structured payload.
